newsitem.title: BELGIUM: AEA airlines' traffic up 10.5 pct yr/yr in January.
newsitem.headline: AEA airlines' traffic up 10.5 pct yr/yr in January.

text.p: Major European airlines saw passenger traffic rise 10.5 percent year-on-year in January this year, the Association of European Airlines said on Thursday.

"Heading the list of growth areas was the North Atlantic, with plus 13.1 percent. Close behind, with a 12.1 percent increase, was the other major long-haul region, Far East/Australasia," said a statement from the AEA, which represents the major airlines from central and western Europe.
Intra-European services posted a 7.4 percent increase.
Seat occupancy on all routes rose 1.7 percentage points to 66.1 percent, although Europe's bumped along at 51.2 percent.

"Given that a single point of European load factor generates about $320 million in revenue over the course of a year, the ongoing overcapacity in Europe -- a hangover from the recession or a consequence of liberalisation and competition -- remains a cause for concern," the statement said.

AEA added that the airfreight market grew 1.4 percent year-on-year, a reflection of the traditionally quiet month, although the Far Eastern routes remained perky at 7.9 percent, offset by a drop of 6.3 percent in volume on the North Atlantic. -- Brussels Newsroom 32 2 287 6800
